Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the final innings of this Test match! England players are out there in the huddle and they disperse now to take their respective positions. Kraigg Brathwaite and John Campbell are the openers for West Indies. Mark Wood is not on the field and he will not take any further part in this Test match. Chris Woakes to start with the ball for England. Kraigg Brathwaite will be on strike. Here we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS …

England have declared! Quite a bold decision this and West Indies now need 286 runs to win this game. England, on the other hand, have close to 70 overs to bowled out Windies and it will be quite an interesting passage of play before Lunch now. England came with an intent this morning and despite losing wickets kept scoring runs at the brisk interval and added 132 runs in their tally. The skipper. Joe Root got to his century and other chipped in with handy cameos. Windies bowlers were decent tough and got wickets at regular intervals. However, it remains to be seen now how their batting group reacts to this total. The match is poised quite nicely now and we are in for some thrilling action as both teams will be eager to get those crucial WTC points on the board. Stay tuned for the final innings of this Test match!
FOUR! Short delivery this time and it provides a boundary! A short delivery on middle. Bairstow pulls it fine towards long leg for a boundary.
This time full on middle. Woakes makes room and drills it to long on for a single.
A length delivery, on off. Woakes makes room and pushes it to long off for a single.
This time it is full again but on middle. Woakes works it towards mid-wicket.
Goes fuller on off. Bairstow drives it to long off for a single.
A length delivery, on middle. Bairstow blocks it out.
This time it is fuller on middle. Woakes works it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Good shot this time! A fullish delivery on middle and leg. Woakes clips it fine towards long leg for a boundary.
A length delivery on off. Woakes punches it to long on for a single.
Another length delivery, around off. Jonny Bairstow pushes it to deep cover for a single.
A length delivery, on off. Bairstow blocks it out.

Fuller and down the leg side this time. Jonny Bairstow looks to flick it but misses.
A length ball, on off. Bairstow pushes it to covers.

Back of a length, on off. Woakes pushes it towards covers for a single.

Drifting on the pads again. Fuller this time. Woakes flicks it to deep square leg for a single.
A full delivery on middle. Woakes works it towards the deep mid-wicket region for a couple.
A fullish delivery, on off. Woakes drives it back to the bowler.
A full delivery on leg. Bairstow flicks it to fine leg for a single.
A length delivery, outside off. Woakes lets it go this time.
A length delivery, outside off. Jonny Bairstow steers it towards third man for a single.
A fullish delivery, on off. Jonny Bairstow blocks it out.

Drinks! This has been an entertaining morning. Five wickets and plenty of runs scored as well. So things are getting quite interesting here and it remains to be seen how much more England score before they declare or get bowled out here. An interesting passage of play coming up. He sees Root getting across here and serves this very full on middle and leg. Root misses and the ball shatters the stumps. So Windies are chipping in with wickets and with lead now 246 batters will continue to keep going here. End of another supern knock by the English skipper, truly deserves all the applauds.

We are all set to begin on Day 5! West Indies players are out there in the middle and Zak Crawley and Joe Root also walk out to the middle now to resume their innings. Nkrumah Bonner will also resume his over which was interrupted by rain on Day 4. Here we go...

The pitch has been pretty unresponsive for the bowlers while the batters have also struggled to score quickly due to the slow nature of the pitch. The conditions are expected to be more or less the same on the final day and Windies will need a special bowling effort in the first session of the day to garner any hopes of winning this Test. England, on the other hand, need to step on the gas and would be looking to add at least 100 runs to their kitty before they can think of declaring and having a crack at the Windies' batting lineup. The rain played spoilsport in the final session of Day 4 and let us hope that it stays away on this final day. An interesting first session coming up. Stay tuned for further updates.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 5 of this first Test between West Indies and England. We are into the final day of this Test match but one must say that the game has not progressed at a pace where we can say that we will surely get a winner at the end of this Test match. At this point in time, a draw seems the most likely result but cricket is a funny game and we have seen Test matches take some exciting turns on the final day. England had a productive Day 4 as they wrapped up the Windies innings in the first over of the day itself and then Zak Crawley and Root made sure that they lost only one wicket throughout the day and eventually ended with a lead of 153 runs. England look like the more liklier of the two teams coming into the final day to push for a win and let's see how things pan out on the final day of this Test match.
...Day 5, Session 1...

Right then! Day 4 was interrupted by rain and we hope that it stays away on the final day of this Test match. We are in for an exciting finish to this Test as all three results are still possible, however, draw seems to be the most likely of them. The final day will begin half an hour early i.e. at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT). But as usual, the build-up will begin well in advance. Do join us for the same. Cheers!

Zak Crawley is up for a quick chat. He says that he enjoyed batting out in the middle and also credits Joe Root for the way he batted alongside him. Mentions that they will give themselves a chance in the morning on Day 5 and says, they still have a chance of winning this Test.

West Indies toiled hard. They managed to pick just one wicket, that too very early on and after that, there was nothing much for them. Although, the pitch is dead and not supportive, their bowlers were a bit widish and did not create enough sustaining pressure while Veerasammy Permaul was taken to cleaners. West Indies will be grateful that rain came in late and the tired minds can push on the final day of this Test match. England, on the other hand, have already lost some overs today and it is very dubious for a result but anything can happen in a Test match.

Just a quick glance at how the day went. England bossed the day thoroughly. They did well to take the last Windies wicket quickly and started their proceedings with intent. However, Alex Lees fell in the process but since then the visitors bossed each and every session. Zak Crawley and Joe Root combined to build a partnership of 193 runs. Crawley has notched up his second Test century while the skipper alongside, is also looking for a triple-digit score. England came into the final session with much more aggression as they scored more boundaries and did not allow the spinners to ease up. They were on a good course but the rain interruptions came unplanned in between.

Length ball, outside off, stays low again. Root misses his cut.
On middle. Root pushes it nicely, straight back but Joseph blocks it with his boots.
Touch fuller and on off. Root mistimes his push back to the bowler.
Fuller ball, outside off, skidding through and stays low while coming back in. Root misses his push.
Length ball, outside off, hint of inswing. Root covers his stump and lets it through.
Fuller and on middle. Zak keeps it out.
Tossed up, on middle. Defended out.
Tossed up, on off. Crawley lunges and blocks it out.
Fuller and around off. Root paddles it to fine leg for a single. A 150-run stand between these two.
Shorter and outside off. Root pushes off the back foot to point.
FOUR! England have just put a shift to the gears! Tossed up, on middle. Root gets low and sweeps it to square leg for a boundary.
On a length, around off. Zak Crawley dabs it onto the deck.
FOUR! SMASHED! Short and wide, outside off. Zak Crawley stays back and slaps it through the point region to bag another boundary. He moves on to 94 now!
FOUR! Streaky! A full ball, outside off and enticing the batter to drive. Zak Crawley throws his bat at it and the ball goes well over the slip cordon for a boundary.

A short ball, around off. Zak Crawley mistimes his pull towards the mid on fielder, along the ground.
A length ball, around middle. Joe Root tucks it around the corner and rotates the strike.
Flatter ball, on middle. Root nudges it to the leg side and takes a run. He will retain the strike.

FOUR! Drops it a bit short this time and Root is too good a player to miss out on a scoring opportunity! Flatter and quicker, outside off. Root stays back and cuts it past the backward point fielder for a boundary.
A length ball, darted on the pads. Zak Crawley tucks it around the corner and takes off for a quick run.
Flatter ball, on a length, around middle. Zak Crawley blocks it off the back foot.
FOUR! Veerasammy Permaul continues to struggle with his line and length! This is a full ball, down leg. Zak Crawley gets down on his knee and sweeps it through the fine leg region to bag a boundary.

Good-length delivery, around middle. Zak Crawley flicks it to deep mid-wicket and comes back for the second run.

Fuller in length, outside off. Zak Crawley lets it through to the keeper.
Joseph bends his back and serves a bumper, around off. Root swivels and pulls it along the ground towards deep square leg for a single.
Back of a length, around off. Root hangs back and blocks it solidly onto the deck.
Joseph starts with a length ball, outside off. Joe Root leaves it alone.
We are back for the final session. The players are out in the middle.  Zak Crawley and Joe Root to continue their innings. Alzarri Joseph to steam in...
...Day 4, Session 3...

West Indies though would be disappointed as nothing has gone their way so far on Day 4, except the wicket of Alex Lees. Their bowlers have toiled hard but to no avail. The pacers have been a tad inconsistent in the middle session and their spinner, Veerasammy Permaul has looked completely out of sorts so far in this innings. The hosts now need wickets in quick succession if they are to restrict the scoring. Do join us for the last session of Day 4 which begins at 1.00 am IST (7.30 pm GMT, previous day).

Another session that has been dominated by England! They have stretched the lead to 82, without losing a wicket in the middle session and the partnership between Root and Crawley is now 122! Both of them got to their fifties in this session and they are looking well-set to get a big one here. England are making sure that they get to a position from where they can't lose this Test.
Floated, full and on middle. Crawley presses forward to block it. That will be Tea on Day 4.
Tossed up, full and on middle, pushed to mid-wicket.

Flatter and on middle. Root on the back foot, nudges it to square leg for one.

FOUR! Shorter and outside off. Crawley cuts it hard and to point for a boundary.

NOT OUT! Zak Crawley survives! This is a full ball, around middle and leg. Crawley looks to play it across the line but he gets an inside edge and the ball ricochets off his boot, onto the pad and then lobs up towards the first slip fielder who grabs it. West Indies appeal but the umpire is not sure and he refers it upstairs. The replays roll in and it shows that the ball bounced off the surface after hitting the inside edge and then went on to hit the boot of Crawley. West Indies players aren't happy with the decision though!

An appeal for a catch and the umpire just asks the players to hold their celebration. Soft-signal is not out. UltraEdge shows a big spike on it. Means definitely bat there but the ball bounces before hitting the boot. NOT OUT it is.

Tossed up, down leg. Zak Crawley reaches out, kneels and sweeps it behind square on the leg side without much timing for a couple of runs.

Another loopy ball, full and on middle. Zak Crawley dabs it onto the deck.

Good tag team effort from Alzarri Joseph and Jason Holder! This is a full ball, outside off. Zak Crawley drives it past mid off. Floated, on a length and going on with the arm, from middle. Joe Root taps it towards point and settles for a single.

... Day 4, Session 2 ...

England are in the lead now and West Indies need to make sure that they make some early inroads post Lunch, as this partnership can take the game away for them. We are in for another exciting session and the middle session will begin at 10.20 pm IST (4.50 pm GMT). Do join us then.

Earlier in the session, it was Jack Leach who wrapped things up quickly for England as he took the last Windies wicket in the very first over of Day 4, and then it was onto the English batters to see off the new ball and provide their team a good start. The debutant, Alex Lees once again perished early but his partner, Zak Crawley along with Joe Root batted really well and they have ensured that they do not lose any more wickets heading into the Lunch break. West Indies started well with the ball, as their veteran, Kemar Roach got rid of Alex Lees and he was the pick of the bowler yet again for the hosts. Veerasammy Permaul was introduced just before the break but he leaked some runs as Crawley didn't allow him to settle in.

End of a riveting first session on Day 4! West Indies' pacers continued to ask some serious questions with the new ball but the pair of Root and Crawley have weathered the storm well so far and have made sure that they do not repeat the mistakes that they did in the first innings. The tourists now lead by 8 runs and would be reasonably happy going into the Lunch break, having cut down the deficit at the cost of just one wicket.
Length and on middle. Crawley blocks it solidly. England lead by 8 runs. That will be Lunch on Day 4.
A length ball, nipping in around off. Crawley defends it.
Outside off. Left alone.

Fuller now, on middle, flicked to deep square leg for a single.
FOUR! Edgy! A length ball, outside off. Root looks to defend with an angled bat but gets an outside edge past the first slip and to the third man fence.
Might be the last over before Lunch.
Fuller in length, around middle. Zak Crawley prods and tucks it to mid-wicket.

Full and around off. Joe Root prods and flicks it to mid-wicket.

FOUR! Too short and Zak Crawley makes full use of it! A half-tracker, outside off. Crawley sits back in his crease and smacks it through the cover region for a boundary.
Tosses it up, around off. Crawley prods to defend but the ball goes off the outer half of the bat towards point.
Slightly short and outside off. Zak Crawley rocks back and slaps it through point for a brace.
Time for some spin as Veerasammy Permaul comes into the attack now.

Follows with a solid block on the off side.

Length and down the leg side. Root tickles it to fine leg for a single. Too many deliveries going down the leg side.
Length and on middle. Blocked out.

Length ball, well wide outside off. Easily left.
Length and outside off. Crawley shoulders arms to that one.
Fuller ball, on middle. Crawley drives it hard and to mid on where Kemar Roach makes a good stop.
Length ball, around off. Crawley drops it to point.
On a length, outside off. Defended out.
Down the leg side. Crawley misses his flick.
Starts with a fuller ball, on middle. Root whips it to deep square leg for a single.
Alzarri Joseph comes into the attack.
FOUR! Short of a length, on middle. Crawley pulls it, does not time it well but hits it well wide of the fielder at deep square leg.

Around off. Kept out.

Jayden Seales (3-1-10-0) is back on.

DRINKS! West Indies have started well with the ball yet again! Roach has been bowling probing lines and lengths and has troubled Zak Crawley a fair bit. Although, Crawley hasn't thrown away his wicket and he must now ensure that he bats deep along with his skipper, Joe Root who has joined him in the middle, just minutes before the Drinks break.

Review! West Indies opt for a review after a lot of discussion. Zak Crawley has been struck on his pad. No bat involved, confirms the UltraEdge. The Ball Tracker rolls in and it suggests that the impact is outside the off pole. West Indies lose a review.

NOT OUT! A fuller ball, coming in with the angle, around off. Crawley takes a step across and looks to defend but gets beaten on the inside edge and gets hit on the pad. A stifled appeal for LBW but nothing given. After plenty of thinking, Kraigg Brathwaite takes the review. And he has lost the review because the impact is outside off, as suggested by the Ball Tracker. So, both the team lose one review early on.

On a length, around off. Root hops and blocks it out.
Length ball, outside off. Left alone.
Joe Root walks in at number 3.

OUT! LBW! West Indies get the breakthrough and Roach gets Lees LBW again in this match. Very similar wicket to the first innings. Roach comes 'round the wicket and serves a full ball, angling in around middle and leg. Alex Lees looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pad. An appeal and up goes the finger. That looked plumb but Lees thought it might go on with the angle and miss leg, so he reviews it. Bu the Ball Tracking shows three reds and Lees has to make a long walk back.
Review! Alex Lees reviews it straightaway after being adjudged LBW! Was there any bat involved? No, says the UltraEdge. Three reds on the Ball Tracker and Kemar Roach gets the breakthrough.
Holder bowls it full and outside off. Zak Crawley leaves it alone for the keeper to collect it.
Much fuller and around off. Zak Crawley keeps it out, off the front foot.
Good-length delivery, well outside off. Zak Crawley shoulders his arms at this one.
On a length, around off. Alex Lees taps it to the off side and rotates the strike.
That came back in sharply! Fuller in length, nipping back in from middle. Alex Lees prods to flick it but he misses and gets hit on his front pad.
A full ball, jagging back in from outside off. Alex Lees prods and lets it sail through to the keeper.
A full ball, well outside off. Zak Crawley does not bother playing at it.
Pitches it up, around off. Zak Crawley keeps it out off the front foot.
BEAUTY! Another ball, that jags away late after pitching just outside off. Zak Crawley looks to block off the front foot but the ball zips past his outside edge. This is brilliant bowling from Roach!
BEATEN! This is a good-length delivery, just outside off. Zak Crawley has a poke at it but the ball nips away a bit and beats his outside edge.
On a length, around middle. Zak Crawley prods and flicks it with soft hands, along the ground towards square leg.
Fuller in length, on middle and leg. Zak Crawley flicks it behind square on the leg side and comes back for the second run.
Holder changes his angle and comes over the wicket this time. A length ball, around off. Lees prods and defends it.
Back of a length, angling in from outside off. Alex Lees hangs back to flick but he misses and gets hit on his body.
Much fuller this time, outside off. Alex Lees gets forward and defends it to the off side.
Pitches it up, around the fourth stump channel. Alex Lees prods to block it out.
A bit fuller this time, angling in from middle. Alex Lees misses his flick and gets hit low on his pad.
Holder comes 'round the wicket and starts with a length ball, angling in from outside off. Alex Lees leaves it alone.
First change of the innings. Jason Holder is brought into the attack. 2 slips and a gully.
A full ball, on middle. Zak Crawley gets forward and flicks it to mid-wicket.
Well bowled! This is a good-length ball, outside off and angling in late. Zak Crawley looks to defend off the front foot but he cleverly gets his bat away from the line of the ball.
Good-length delivery, just outside off. Zak Crawley prods and keeps it out.
On a length, around off. Zak Crawley leans and blocks it out.
Roach serves a length ball, nipping back in from off. Zak Crawley gets forward and flicks it from the inner half of his bat towards deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
A full ball, around off. Alex Lees prods and defends it to the off side. The batters cross ends.
Back of a length, outside off. Zak Crawley lets it sail through to the keeper.
Another ball, full and outside off. Zak Crawley leaves it alone.
An overpitched ball, outside off. Crawley offers no shot and watches the ball closely.
Good-length ball, well outside off. Zak Crawley gets forward and lets it through to the keeper.
FOUR! Lovely timing! A full ball, angling in from middle. Zak Crawley prods and flicks it nonchalantly through the mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Good-length ball, around off. Zak Crawley keeps it out.
Good-length ball, outside off. Alex Lees leaves it alone watchfully.
A length ball, angling down leg. Alex Lees misses his flick and the ball goes through to the keeper.
Another full ball, way outside off. Alex Lees leaves it alone.
Fuller in length, around leg. Zak Crawley tickles it towards fine leg and takes a single.
A full ball, outside off. Zak Crawley gets forward and drives it back to the bowler.
A stifled appeal for caught behind but it clearly came off the pad. A length ball, angling down leg. Zak Crawley misses his flick and the ball brushes his pad before going to the keeper.
A full ball, around leg. Zak Crawley flicks it through the mid-wicket region and the batters collect three runs.
Seales goes full and outside off. Zak Crawley leaves it alone.
Nicely played! Shorter in length, outside off. Alex Lees rides the bounce and punches it through the cover region. The batters take three runs.
Short of a length, outside off. Alex Lees offers no shot to that one.
Good-length ball, just outside off. Alex Lees prods but does not bother playing at it.
On a length, outside off. Alex Lees shoulders his arms at this one.
Back of a length, well outside off. Zak Crawley lets it sail through to the keeper.
Fuller in length, outside off. Zak Crawley looks to defend but it goes off the thick outside edge, and rolls past the gully fielder for a couple of runs.
Fuller in length, outside off. Zak Crawley leaves it for the keeper to collect.
FOUR! Easy pickings! First boundary of the innings! Roach persists with full-length stuff but strays on the pads this time. Crawley flicks it behind square on the leg side and bags a boundary.
This is on a length, well outside off. Zak Crawley lets it sail through.
Good-length ball, around off. Zak Crawley blocks it off the front foot.
Full and on middle. Lees keeps it out.
Back of a length, angling across the batter. Alex Lees does not bother playing at it.
On a length, just outside off. Alex Lees shoulders his arms at this one.
Seales pitches it up, just outside off. Lees gets forward and defends it.
Good-length ball, around off. Alex Lees prods and blocks it towards cover.
A full ball, outside off. Alex Lees leaves it alone.
Jayden Seales to bowl from the other end.

NOT OUT! Zak Crawley survives and this is a smart review by the Englishman after consulting with Lees! A length ball, nipping back in from middle. Crawley gets across and looks to flick it but he misses and gets pinged on his pad. West Indies appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Crawley reviews and the Ball Tracker shows that the ball would have gone down leg. England retain their review.

Review! Zak Crawley went to Alex Lees and asked if that is going down and goes upstairs to change the LBW decision. No bat clearly there and Ball Tracking shows the ball is missing the stumps by quite some distance.
A full ball, outside off. Crawley lets it through to the keeper.
A length ball, around middle. Zak Crawley flicks it to mid-wicket. Not in the gap though!
Good-length ball, around off. Lees hangs back and taps it to the off side. He scampers through to the other end. England and Lees are underway!
BEATEN! Roach serves another full ball, outside off, enticing the batter to drive. Lees looks to drive but the ball zips past his outside edge.
Roach starts with a full ball, outside off. Alex Lees leaves it alone.
